newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU industry output growth slows to 0.3 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: EU industry output growth slows to 0.3 pct in 1996.

text.p: Industrial production increased by only 0.3 percent in the European Union last year, sharply down from its 3.8 percent rise in 1995, Eurostat reported on Friday.
The early estimate from Eurostat, the European Union's statistics office, was based on production indices for total industry available up to last November.
It indicated the Netherlands showed the best result, almost doubling its growth last year to 4.4 percent from 2.4 percent in 1995.
Finland's output growth slowed to 2.3 percent from 7.5 percent while Sweden's increase was 2.1 percent, down from 10 percent the previous year.
"Belgium, Germany and France recorded weak growth," Eurostat said in a statement.

Three countries -- Spain, Italy and Luxembourg -- showed declining industrial production in 1996. Italy's output fell by 2.3 percent while Spain's and Luxembourg's figures both declined by 0.9 percent compared with 1995.
